incoming.explanation: The inventory's 'Quinapaug wch we know not' line is the primary evidence for the unvalued frontier interest.
The Suffolk Deeds Quinapaug conveyances locate the tract in the Providence jurisdiction and show no recorded Gurney parcel, grounding the unrecorded-share reading of the estate line.
The unvalued Quinapaug interest is the third leg of the frontier-rights pattern.
Framing the estate as otherwise all personalty makes the lone unvalued Quinapaug land line (frontier-rights) legible as the single land asset the appraisers could not price.
Cross-unit: the silent Providence records bound John's unrecorded Quinapaug (Providence-jurisdiction) frontier share.

finding.shortLabel: Finding: Quinapaug line = unrecorded Providence-jurisdiction frontier share
finding.statement: The 1663 inventory's 'estate layd out in land at Quinapaug wch we know not' is best read as an unrecorded right or share in the Providence-jurisdiction Quinapaug land speculation (Foote to Hudson to Boston men) - an unvalued frontier proprietary interest, not appraised Braintree real estate.

finding.statement: John Gurney's 1663 Braintree probate inventory (taken 16 March 1663; total 55 pounds 14s 6d) records a land-interest line reading 'an estate layd out in land at Quinapaug wch we know not' - an interest the appraisers could not value.

outgoing.explanation: The Suffolk Deeds Quinapaug conveyances locate the tract in the Providence jurisdiction and show no recorded Gurney parcel, grounding the unrecorded-share reading of the estate line.

finding.shortLabel: Suffolk Deeds IV - Quinapaug (Providence-jurisdiction) tract, no Gurney in the recorded deeds

sources.alignmentNote: No Gurney among the recorded Quinapaug deeds (pp. 268, 270-271 per the volume index).
sources.locator: Suffolk Deeds Lib. IV pp. 270-271 read via FamilySearch full-text images, film 007442495, image 191 (Hudson to Button; recites Foote's 18 June 1655 Indian purchase and the 1660 conveyance to Hudson)

finding.statement: Suffolk Deeds Liber IV records the Quinapaug tract: Joshua Foote bought 4,000 acres 'att Quinapaug within ye Jurisdiction of Providence' from the Indians Sacont and George Sacount by deed of 18 June 1655; by 1660 it passed to William Hudson, who sold it in 500-acre parcels to Boston men. No Gurney appears among the recorded Quinapaug parcels.
